steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the 'https' and 'util' modules from Node.js core.
steps.hint: Use the 'require' statement to import Node.js built-in modules. Both modules are available globally in Node.js.
steps.expectedOutcome: The 'https' and 'util' modules are imported and ready to use for making HTTP requests and promisifying functions.
successCriteria: The 'https' and 'util' modules are imported using require statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported both required Node.js modules. The 'https' module will handle HTTP requests, and 'util' will help promisify callback-style functions.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one module, but both 'https' and 'util' are needed. Make sure to import both using separate require statements.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import both 'https' and 'util' modules using require statements.

steps.title: Create the retryWithJitter function skeleton
steps.instruction: Define a function named retryWithJitter that accepts four parameters: url, options, maxRetries, and baseDelay. The function should return a promise.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Remember to include the parameters in parentheses and return a promise (e.g., return new Promise(...)).

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the retryWithJitter function skeleton with all required parameters.

steps.title: Implement the exponential backoff calculation
steps.instruction: Inside the retryWithJitter function, create a helper function called calculateDelay that takes retryCount and baseDelay as parameters and returns the exponential backoff delay using the formula 2^retryCount * baseDelay.
steps.hint: The helper function should be defined inside retryWithJitter. Use Math.pow(2, retryCount) or the exponentiation operator (**) to calculate 2^retryCount, then multiply by baseDelay.
steps.expectedOutcome: A calculateDelay helper function is defined inside retryWithJitter, correctly implementing the exponential backoff formula.
successCriteria: The calculateDelay function exists, takes retryCount and baseDelay parameters, and returns 2^retryCount * baseDelay.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the exponential backoff calculation helper function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a helper function, but check the formula. It should be 2^retryCount * baseDelay.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateDelay helper function is missing or incorrect. It should take retryCount and baseDelay and return the exponential backoff delay.

steps.title: Add jitter to the delay calculation
steps.instruction: Inside the calculateDelay function, modify the delay calculation to add random jitter by multiplying the base delay by a random factor between 0.5 and 1.5.
steps.hint: Use Math.random() to generate a random number between 0 and 1, then scale it to the desired range and multiply it with the base delay.
steps.expectedOutcome: The calculateDelay function now returns a delay with random jitter applied, helping to prevent the thundering herd problem.
successCriteria: The calculateDelay function multiplies the baseDelay by a random factor between 0.5 and 1.5.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added jitter to the delay calculation. This helps distribute retry attempts more evenly.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're multiplying the baseDelay by a random factor between 0.5 and 1.5.
steps.feedbackWrong: The jitter calculation isn't quite right. Remember to multiply the baseDelay by a random factor between 0.5 and 1.5.

steps.title: Create the HTTP request helper function
steps.instruction: Inside the retryWithJitter function, create a helper function named makeRequest that accepts a url parameter and returns a promise wrapping an https.request call.
steps.hint: Use the https module's request method inside a new Promise constructor. The promise should resolve with the response data or reject with an error.
steps.expectedOutcome: The retryWithJitter function now contains a makeRequest helper function that returns a promise for HTTP requests.
successCriteria: A makeRequest function is defined inside retryWithJitter, accepts a url parameter, and returns a new Promise.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the promise-based HTTP request helper function.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure makeRequest accepts a url parameter and returns a new Promise.
steps.feedbackWrong: The makeRequest function should be defined inside retryWithJitter and return a promise for HTTP requests.

steps.title: Implement the retry loop logic
steps.instruction: Inside the retryWithJitter function, add a for loop that attempts the request and retries on failure up to maxRetries.
steps.hint: Use a for loop that iterates from 0 to maxRetries. Inside the loop, call the makeRequest helper function and handle success or failure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The retryWithJitter function now contains a for loop that will attempt the request multiple times with exponential backoff and jitter.
successCriteria: A for loop is added inside retryWithJitter that iterates up to maxRetries, calls makeRequest, and handles retries on failure.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the retry loop logic. This forms the core of the retry mechanism.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the loop structure or error handling needs adjustment. Make sure the loop handles both success and failure cases properly.
steps.feedbackWrong: The retry loop logic is missing or incorrect. Review the example and ensure you've added a proper for loop inside the retryWithJitter function.

steps.title: Add delay between retry attempts
steps.instruction: Inside the retry loop in your retryWithJitter function, add a delay using setTimeout wrapped in a promise before making the next retry attempt. Wait for the calculated jittered delay.
steps.hint: Create a promise that resolves after the delay using setTimeout. Use the calculateDelay function to get the wait time for the current attempt.
steps.expectedOutcome: The retry loop will include a delay before each retry attempt, using the jittered exponential backoff calculation.
successCriteria: The retry loop contains a promise-based delay using setTimeout that waits for the calculated jittered delay before the next retry attempt.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the delay mechanism between retry attempts using promises and setTimeout.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using setTimeout wrapped in a promise and waiting for the calculated delay from the calculateDelay function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The delay implementation is missing or incorrect. Remember to create a promise that resolves after the calculated delay using setTimeout.

steps.title: Handle successful responses
steps.instruction: Inside the makeRequest helper function, add logic to return the response data when the HTTP request succeeds (status code 200-299).
steps.hint: Check if response.statusCode is between 200 and 299, then collect and return the response data.
steps.expectedOutcome: The makeRequest function will properly handle successful HTTP responses by returning the response data.
successCriteria: The makeRequest function checks for status codes 200-299 and returns the parsed response data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the success handling logic for HTTP responses.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure to check the status code range and properly collect/return the response data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The success handling logic is missing or incorrect. Review how to check HTTP status codes and process response data.

steps.title: Handle final failure after all retries
steps.instruction: Inside the retryWithJitter function, after the retry loop, add logic to throw an error when all retry attempts have been exhausted without success.
steps.hint: After the loop completes without returning a successful response, you can throw a new Error with a descriptive message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The retryWithJitter function should now properly handle the case where all retry attempts fail by throwing a descriptive error.
successCriteria: An error is thrown with a descriptive message when maxRetries is reached without a successful response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've properly implemented error handling for when all retry attempts fail. This ensures the function provides clear feedback when it cannot complete the request.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're throwing an Error object with a descriptive message about the retry failure.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should throw an error when all retry attempts have been exhausted. Look at the analogous example for guidance on error handling after a retry loop.

steps.title: Export the retryWithJitter function
steps.instruction: Export the retryWithJitter function using module.exports so it can be imported and used in other modules.
steps.hint: Add a module.exports statement at the end of your file to export the function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The retryWithJitter function will be available for import in other Node.js modules.
successCriteria: The retryWithJitter function is exported using module.exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the retryWithJitter function. It's now ready to be imported and used in other modules.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close, but the export isn't quite right. Make sure you're using module.exports to export the retryWithJitter function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The retryWithJitter function isn't properly exported. Check that you're using module.exports to make the function available to other modules.
